Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor (GIST): cytoplasmic positivity for KIT protein and CD34
Neoplastic cells: diffuse and marked cytoplasmic positivity for KIT protein and CD34 in the majority of cells
Histological examination: proliferation of densely packed spindle cells with prominent nuclear palisading
Total body CT scan: no lymph node enlargement nearby or distant metastases, mass appeared circumscribed and did not infiltrate surrounding tissues
Rectal examination: well-defined mass on the left-anterior aspect of the anal canal, starting 1 cm from the anal verge and extending cranially for approximately 4 cm

top_diagnoses.reasoning_summary: The patient's histological examination and immunohistochemical results are consistent with GIST, including spindle cell morphology, nuclear palisading, and cytoplasmic positivity for KIT protein and CD34. The absence of nuclear atypia, low mitotic count, and well-defined mass with circumscribed margins also support this diagnosis.
